history.p: In the autumn of 1845 the German poet and suffragist Louise Otto published three articles in Neue Zeitschrift für Musik with the title "Die Nibelungen als Oper". She wanted to create a national German opera based on German historical themes. Together with an Austrian poet she decided to write an opera text in two parts: "Der Nibelungen Hort" and "Der Nibelungen Noth". The Austrian never fulfilled his part of the project, with the excuse that he could not find a suited composer; however, Gade must have read Louise Otto's articles, for she later reported to the editor of NZfM, Franz Brendel, that Gade had asked her to write the text of which the first act was published in December 1845, again in NZfM. Gade started setting it to music in January 1847, but never finished the opera.
